topic: Web Development Fundamentals and Internet Basics
learningObjectives: Explain how websites and web applications work.
Identify the roles of browsers, servers, DNS, HTTP, and databases.
Trace a basic request from a browser to a web server and back.

activities.title: Web Architecture Map
activities.instruction: Explore the major parts of a web application and identify what each one does.

content.concept: A web application connects a browser, network, server, application logic, APIs, and databases to deliver functionality.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Requests and displays web resources for the user.
Translates a domain name such as example.com into an IP address.
Receives HTTP requests and serves web resources or forwards requests.
Runs application logic and generates dynamic responses.
Stores and retrieves persistent application data.

activities.title: Request Journey
activities.instruction: Arrange the steps of a browser request from entering a URL to displaying the response.

content.concept: A browser resolves the domain, sends an HTTP request to a server, receives a response, and renders the returned resources.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Web Technology Match
activities.instruction: Identify the role of each core web technology.

content.concept: HTML structures content, CSS controls presentation, JavaScript adds behavior, and servers and databases support application functionality and data.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: HTTP Request Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the main parts of an HTTP request.

content.concept: HTTP requests contain a method, URL, headers, and sometimes a request body used to communicate with servers.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Specifies the intended operation, such as GET or POST.
Carries metadata such as content type or authentication information.
Contains data sent to the server, commonly with POST, PUT, or PATCH requests.
